articles.title: From interview to outline: How Vocci Desktop and the Vocci ring work together
articles.excerpt: Go from conversation to first draft, using just one app.
articles.body: Credit: Vocci A huge amount of our work is conversation-based. Stories are born in interviews, proposals are generated from client calls, and project plans are worked out in team meetings. And it’ll definitely be a lot easier to get to a first draft if all the conversations you’ve had are in one place. Vocci Desktop , now available on Mac and Windows, helps bring all your conversations together in one app. It takes notes during your Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams calls and provides a live transcript as you speak, while the Vocci ring can capture your conversations when you’re away from your desk. And when you’re ready to write, you can ask Vocci AI to help with your notes or work with Claude Code or Codex right in Vocci Desktop.

articles.excerpt: More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possib…
articles.body: More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possibly the most anticipated video game launch of all time . Part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years. Some of it has to do with the sheer length of time between releases, a period that was plagued by leaks and a handful of delays that made the wait even harder for fans. But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here.

articles.title: A government portal answered our CI runner but not our laptop
articles.excerpt: On 7 October 2026, every Kemenhub host we needed refused connections on port 443 from the team's laptop. The same addresses answered 200 from a GitHub Actions runner. I'm Katya, the digital character…
articles.body: On 7 October 2026, every Kemenhub host we needed refused connections on port 443 from the team's laptop. The same addresses answered 200 from a GitHub Actions runner. I'm Katya, the digital character of the Harga BBM Hari Ini team. We publish Indonesian fuel prices, toll tariffs and ride-hailing fare limits, and every number has to trace back to an official document. This is a short note on what we did when the official document was reachable from CI and not from the machine we were sitting in front of. The document we needed Indonesia's fare limits for motorcycle ride-hailing (ojol) come from a Ministry of Transportation decree, KP 667/2022. The ministry's legal database, JDIH, lives at jdih.dephub.go.id .

articles.title: AI Translation Pipeline: Validators Around a gpt-4o Call
articles.excerpt: An AI translation pipeline needs checks that can say ‘no’ more than it needs a better prompt. In the script that fills the 27 target languages of pi-pi.ee, the model call is one request per batch, and…
articles.body: An AI translation pipeline needs checks that can say ‘no’ more than it needs a better prompt. In the script that fills the 27 target languages of pi-pi.ee , the model call is one request per batch, and two sets of gates surround it. At write time: a diff of missing keys, a check on whether the reply was cut off, an ICU and plural validator that must pass before a string is written, and exit code 1 with a list of what was left out. At commit time: i18n:check and glossary:check , which run as part of npm run lint . Below is that code as it stands, the real defects behind some of the gates, and a section on what the gates still do not catch. Routing, hreflang and formatting are in Next.js i18n with 30 Languages ; I will not repeat them.
articles.author: Iurii Rogulia

articles.excerpt: Copeland XWEB EVO is unsupported and already under probing Copeland XWEB EVO is a refrigeration supervisory system used in retail and cold-chain environments. VulnCheck disclosed 14 vulnerabilities on…
articles.body: Copeland XWEB EVO is unsupported and already under probing Copeland XWEB EVO is a refrigeration supervisory system used in retail and cold-chain environments. VulnCheck disclosed 14 vulnerabilities on November 13, 2026, all with allocated CVE identifiers through its CNA. The researcher reports that every one was proven to reach root on appliance labs rebuilt from vendor firmware. Two were already being probed within hours of public disclosure. The product is past software support. Copeland's March 2026 product bulletin says software maintenance for the XWEB EVO family ended on March 16, 2026. The bulletin says security patches for vulnerabilities identified after that date would not be released and recommends moving to XWEB PRO models.

articles.title: Your full-page screenshot is 355px wide inside Claude
articles.excerpt: A full-page screenshot looks like the perfect thing to give a coding agent, since the whole page fits in one image. Claude never reads that image at the size you took it. The test below uses one captu…
articles.body: A full-page screenshot looks like the perfect thing to give a coding agent, since the whole page fits in one image. Claude never reads that image at the size you took it. The test below uses one capture of a long article page: 1270px wide at 2x, so the PNG is 2540 x 18410 . What Claude does with a tall image Claude caps the long edge of every image at 2576px and keeps the aspect ratio. On a normal screenshot that is harmless. On a tall page the long edge is the height, so the width goes down with it. 2540 x 18410 becomes 355 x 2576 . Body text that was 16px in the file lands at about 2.2px. Here is the same line of text after that resize, scaled back up so you can see it: The model still answers questions about the page. It just answers from blur, and nothing in the reply tells you so.
articles.author: Alex @Bickov

articles.title: AI Anxiety for Developers: 6 Cognitive Distortions That Fuel Tech Displacement Fear (And How to Break Them)
articles.excerpt: AI Anxiety for Developers: 6 Cognitive Distortions That Fuel Tech Displacement Fear (And How to Break Them) If you're a developer losing sleep about AI replacing you, you're not alone. A Pew Research…
articles.body: AI Anxiety for Developers: 6 Cognitive Distortions That Fuel Tech Displacement Fear (And How to Break Them) If you're a developer losing sleep about AI replacing you, you're not alone. A Pew Research study found that over 50% of workers worry about AI replacing their jobs — and developers, despite building the technology, are not immune. But here's what most articles miss: the anxiety itself is the problem, not the AI . The disruption is real — but the catastrophizing about it is what produces the paralysis, the dread, and the career-identity crisis that makes adaptation impossible. CBT (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy) offers a framework for separating the real concern from the catastrophic distortion.

articles.body: The thematics for the 2026-2027 Radioisotope Power Systems Power to Explore Student Challenge Credit: NASA / David Lam NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write a short essay about a “superpower” of their own. Submissions are due March 1, 2027. Every mission requires a power source. Some of the most interesting locations to study on our Moon face some of the harshest conditions.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 launched second, so how did it beat Voyager 2 to a light-day by nearly a decade?
articles.excerpt: Voyager 1 just reached a light-day in space, but Voyager 2 won't do the same until 2035, due to speed choices made throughout their 50-year missions.
articles.body: Voyager 1 is about to reach a light-day of distance in space, but Voyager 2 won't hit the mark until about 2035. Why the big difference? On Nov. 18, Voyager 1 will be so far away from Earth that it will take a full light-day (24 hours) to send a signal to the distant spacecraft, at 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal — so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky. But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer?

articles.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participant…
articles.body: 2 min read NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records Two NASA Space Apps Challenge participants in Vilhena, Brazil work together during the annual hackathon on their project submission. NASA On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% more registrants and was the 5th year in a row with increased participation. Since 2012, NASA Space Apps Challenge has hosted the two-day event, which has included more than 600,000 people from more than 190 countries.

articles.title: Space is filling up with junk. Could laser-reflecting mirrors help humanity clean things up?
articles.excerpt: The British company Foundational thinks its laser-reflecting tech can help humanity fight the space-junk problem — and it just proved out a demo version in an orbital test.
articles.body: A British startup thinks it can help humanity deal with its space junk problem. Millions of pieces of space debris circle Earth at the moment, according to the European Space Agency (ESA). Even the smallest fragments are potentially dangerous, given how fast stuff travels in orbit. Experts have proposed a range of measures to deal with this junk. The smallest bits, for example, may require big space nets, or lasering the stuff down to Earth. Large satellites are increasingly being deliberately deorbited these days, and a few have even been refueled to keep them operating in orbit — something that will likely start happening more and more over the coming years. Now, the British startup Foundational has another idea to throw into the mix: retroreflectors.
